newsitem.title: USA: GM says Q4 earnings exceed estimates.
newsitem.headline: GM says Q4 earnings exceed estimates.

text.p: General Motors Corp said on Monday its fourth quarter 1996 operating earnings exceeded Wall Street's consensus estimate when income tax benefits and other extraordinary items are boiled out.

GM spokeswoman Toni Simonetti said the automaker is telling analysts that it earned about $0.55 a share from operations in the quarter, which excludes most extraordinary items but includes the negative effect of strikes in the United States and Canada.
The First Call consensus estimate was $0.49 a share.
Simonetti said the $0.55 a share figure adjusts GM's tax expense to reflect a more normal rate of about 34 percent. In the fourth quarter, GM actually received a tax benefit of $262 million.

The automaker reported fourth quarter net income from continuing operations of $786 million, or $0.92 a share, which includes the tax gain plus other special items that reduced income by $762 million, or $0.99 a share. GM's income statement listed the strikes, which cost $700 million, or $0.91 a share, as an extraordinary item.
In the year-ago period, GM earned $1.6 billion, or $1.95 a share, from continuing operations. Both years exclude earnings from Electronic Data Systems Corp, which was spun off in June 1996.
GM Chief Financial Officer J. Michael Losh is scheduled to hold a conference call with reporters at about 1115 EST/1615 GMT.
